title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (December 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET — the one month the last-Tuesday rule does not govern, and the first panel to close after the December SEP
source: EST: NOT the publisher's stated last-Tuesday rule, which December has never once obeyed (0 of 5). THE RULE-DERIVED DATE WOULD BE 2027-12-28 AND IT IS WRONG. This session tested four candidate date rules against the five sourced December releases (2021-12-22 Wed, 2022-12-21 Wed, 2023-12-20 Wed, 2024-12-23 Mon, 2025-12-23 Tue) and exactly ONE fits: 'the latest Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday strictly before December 24', which is 5 OF 5. The three competitors fail -- 'latest Mon-Thu before Dec 24' 2 of 5, 'latest weekday on or before Dec 23' 2 of 5, the publisher's own last Tuesday 0 of 5. That rule returns WEDNESDAY 2027-12-22 for 2027. The proposal that created this id called the date 'a single-instance structural analogue' off 2021, the only other Saturday-Christmas year; this session upgrades that assessment, because the analogue and the 5-of-5 rule are INDEPENDENT derivations that return the same day, and 2021's two offsets (rule date minus 6, Christmas minus 3) return it a third and fourth time. THE HONEST RESIDUAL IS STILL A BAND, 2027-12-20 TO 2027-12-23, because the winning rule is fitted in-sample on the same five points it explains. IT HAS A NEAR-TERM OUT-OF-SAMPLE TEST: the rule predicts 2026-12-23 for December 2026, one day off this calendar's own consumer-confidence-2026-12-22 id, scoreable in about fifteen weeks. Editions re-fetched direct 2026-09-06 through 2026-09-08, all serial, each verified against its own 'Source: <Month> <Year> Consumer Confidence Survey' line and 'Updated:' stamp: CCI-Dec-2022 (889,114 bytes, Updated 2022-12-21), CCI-Dec-2023 (1,264,748 bytes, 2023-12-20), CCI-Dec-2024 (898,445 bytes, 2024-12-23) -- byte-identical to the consumer-confidence-2027-11-30 sibling's fetches of the same three documents. CCI-Dec-2021, CCI-Dec-2025 and CCI-Nov-2025 all served the 332,031-byte current-edition landing page instead of the requested edition and are recorded in probe-ref.blocked; their dates are inherited from the consumer-confidence-2026-12-22 lane, not re-verified here. Promote on the November 2027 edition's next-release line, which names December's date 3 of 3 about four weeks ahead -- that is 2027-11-30 (est.), the proposer's own event. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this id's own never-assessed research (2026-09-08) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-12-22.from-consumer-confidence-2027-11-30.json, which is now inert. Its three cautions were re-tested rather than inherited: one is UPGRADED, one HOLDS, one is REFUTED. (1) UPGRADED -- 'this id's date is the weakest in the CB chain'. It is not. A four-rule bake-off found one formulation that fits December 5 of 5 while every competitor fits 2 of 5 or worse, and it returns 2027-12-22 independently of the 2021 Saturday-Christmas analogue the proposal rested on. The date is still an estimate and still a band (12-20 to 12-23), but it is now the answer of a rule with a scoreable out-of-sample test in December 2026, not a single-instance guess. DO NOT rename to consumer-confidence-2027-12-28 -- that is the last-Tuesday date the record refutes 0 for 5. (2) HOLDS -- 'do not inherit November's cut-off arithmetic'. December's stated cut-offs are December 15 (2022), December 14 (2023) and December 16, 2024, re-read from the editions this session, plus December 16 for 2021 and 2025 inherited from the consumer-confidence-2026-12-22 lane. This SETTLES a live disagreement between two lanes: that lane called the cut-off 'a fixed calendar date, not the floating lag', and on the pooled five it is the opposite -- the LAG spans 6 to 7 (span 1) while the DAY OF MONTH spans 14 to 16 (span 2), so December projects from the lag, exactly inverting November's day-of-month anchor. Projection for a 2027-12-22 release: cut-off 2027-12-15 to 2027-12-16. (3) REFUTED, AND THIS IS THE ENTRY'S HEADLINE -- the proposal implied December would behave like its neighbours. It does not. January restates December +0.7 / -2.7 / +4.8 (108.3 to 109.0, 110.7 to 108.0, 104.7 to 109.5, all three read from the January editions' own text). The |delta| spread is 4.1, the WIDEST in the chain against November's 0.2, and +4.8 is the single largest revision the chain has ever sourced. DECEMBER'S FIRST PRINT IS THE LEAST TRUSTWORTHY IN THE CHAIN, the exact inverse of its November neighbour -- and that inversion is itself the strongest evidence yet for the 09-28/10-26/11-30 lanes' shared claim that revision behaviour is a property of the month. (4) A METHOD FINDING THAT APPLIES CHAIN-WIDE. The post-print Christmas corridor reads 8 of 9 narrower than the tape, and unlike November's post-Thanksgiving result it is NOT a half-session artifact -- removing the corridor's two half sessions leaves it at 8 of 9 with six instruments clearing Bonferroni. But a block-permutation test (the same five contiguous blocks, lengths 6/6/6/4/4, placed at random 2000 times) returns p=0.0575 for 8 of 9 and p=0.0490 for six-at-Bonferroni. The per-session Mann-Whitney every lane in this chain uses OVERSTATES any channel whose set is contiguous blocks. Corridor status: marginal, not established. (5) THE CHAIN'S OPEN VIX DISCREPANCY IS CLOSED. The 11-30 lane banked three unexplained second-decimal gaps against the 10-26 lane and could not name the cause; this session reproduces BOTH sides exactly. CBOE's VIX_History.csv carries rows on 32 NYSE holidays in the 2020-12-01 to 2026-09-04 window, so a lane that does not intersect VIX with the equity session calendar includes them. Session-aligned gives Jun 16.70 / Sep 17.20 / Nov 17.25 (the 11-30 lane's figures); the raw file gives 16.73 / 17.17 / 17.21 (the 10-26 lane's). Neither is a bug and the session-aligned reading is the correct one. Five months differ, not three -- January and May do too. A LIVE INSTANCE sits in today's file: a 09/07/2026 row on Labor Day, a day the NYSE was closed. (6) CORRIDOR. Two events are proposed with this PR, both estimates, both load-bearing: christmas-market-closure-2027-12-24 (Christmas Day is a SATURDAY in 2027, so the NYSE observes it on Friday 2027-12-24 and there is NO Christmas Eve half session at all -- verified in this session's own tape, where 2021, the structural twin, jumps 2021-12-23 to 2021-12-27) and opex-2027-12-17 (December quad-witching, third Friday, five days before this print). SAME CHANNEL CAVEAT AS EVERY CB ENTRY: symbols is empty and no house playbook is macro- or sentiment-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing here licenses an entry.
